entities.label: Text
entities.summary:
Jeddah Tower, located in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, is set to be the tallest building in the world upon its completion, anticipated in 2024. Designed by the architectural firm Adrian Smith + Gordon Gill Architecture, this iconic structure is part of a broader urban development initiative that aims to redefine the skyline of Jeddah and elevate its status on the global stage. The tower symbolizes the economic ambitions of Saudi Arabia, particularly in light of Vision 2030, a strategic framework aimed at diversifying the nation’s economy beyond oil dependence.

Construction of Jeddah Tower began in 2013, and the project has faced various challenges, including financial difficulties and a temporary halt in construction in 2018. When completed, the tower will reach a height of over 1,000 meters, surpassing the Burj Khalifa in Dubai, which currently holds the title of the tallest building. The project is expected to include luxury residences, a hotel, office spaces, and observation decks, showcasing cutting-edge engineering and design.

The legacy of Jeddah Tower extends beyond its physical presence; it represents a shift in architectural ambition and urban planning in the Middle East. By setting a new benchmark for skyscrapers, it influences future developments not only in Saudi Arabia but also across the region, prompting other nations to pursue their monumental projects. As a centerpiece of Jeddah's urban landscape, it is likely to become a significant tourist attraction, contributing to the local economy and redefining the cultural identity of the city.

As architect Adrian Smith stated, 'The tower is not just about height; it’s about creating a new urban environment.' This ambition reflects the broader cultural and economic aspirations of a nation poised at the crossroads of tradition and modernity, serving as a beacon of Saudi Arabia's future endeavors in the global arena.
